　そうそう都合のよい機に都合のよろしい手段を思いつくようなら、恐らく朔屋はそもそもこんな海の下の、こんな常識外れの海底洞窟の、こんな絵空事のような状況に迷いこんではいないのである。
lines.english:
Why, indeed?
If Sakuya could think of a convenient escape at such a convenient moment, he would probably never have strayed beneath the sea, into this undersea cave beyond all common sense, into this scene of pure fantasy.

lines.english: Strictly speaking, there was something he wished for desperately. He had spent the day doing dull, fumbling work—though that was usual—then slept a little, or been made to sleep. Afterward he had trudged through a desert and a graveyard of ships, boarded an unfamiliar steel-hulled vessel, descended to this briny seabed, and found himself surrounded by fish-stinking monsters and their lord. A sequence more likely to make one sick than mixing one's drinks. If lukewarm tea or a bowl of ramen had been offered at the end, that would have been one thing. A sword point whose very steel smelled cold was hardly a fitting finish. No, better not finish anything; if it finished him, he'd be cut dead. Amid that fluster, his back growing clammy, the first thing Sakuya thought of—or wished for—was—

At his wits' end, Sakuya committed an oversight beyond the limits of oversight: he took his eyes from the sword point. His gaze drifted to Rui, still leaning against him. Should he complain that she was acting, or marvel at the perfection of her supple waist? He heard the heat of her skin. The palm resting at his chest slid like a gardenia petal and came to rest at her collar. He saw it. Saw it. Could no longer look away.

It might have been wise to keep an eye on Tomosato's sword too. But at that moment, Sakuya saw only Rui's neck. Her neck.

Thus he did not notice the killer's leveled sword point making a peculiar movement. Little nudges, as though indicating something with a stick.
Nor did he notice Rui and Tomosato exchanging deft signals with their eyes, unseen by anyone else.

lines.japanese:
智里が指したの朔屋の、泪が添う腕へ。
　
　泪が返したのは、万事承知の目礼。
　
　朔屋が泪の麗しい首筋に目を奪われている間に───と、するりと。泪の体が朔屋の体から滑った。あまりに自然で滑らかな流れだったから、日頃は不調法な青年をして、自然に応じさせ、泪の体を支える形に。この時朔屋が、それまで一番目を奪われていた部分をつい支えてしまったのも当然だったろう。
　
　つまり、自分の腕で、体を斜交いにするように滑ってきた、泪の首筋だ。

Tomosato indicated Sakuya's arm, against which Rui leaned.
Rui answered with a nod: understood.
While Sakuya's gaze was captured by her beautiful neck, her body slipped from his. So natural, so smooth was the movement that even ordinarily clumsy Sakuya responded instinctively, supporting her. Naturally enough, he supported the part that had most held his attention.
Her neck, as she slid diagonally across him into his arm.

How hopelessly off course could this man be? Rui, who ought to have leaned against him weakly, shifted once more, putting her back against his front. Several moments passed before he realized that the arm he thought was supporting her had wrapped neatly around her neck. Longer still before he understood that she stood exactly between him and Tomosato's sword point. To grasp what that meant fully, he had to wait for the killer's next words.
Tomosato raised his voice.

Her ensuing scream was plainly fabricated. Indeed, it sounded delighted.

lines.japanese: で、その魚怪の前になぜかひょこりと佇む智里がある。
lines.english: And, for some reason, Tomosato popped up before that fish-monster.

lines.japanese: 「ああ馬鹿お前、今あいつに手を出したなら、お前らの姫さんがどうなるかわかんねえだろうが」
lines.english: “Ah, you fool. Lay hands on him now, and who knows what'll happen to your princess?”

lines.japanese: 魚怪の円い、硝子のような眼に浮かんだのは、怒りや敵意ではなく、理不尽の色合いなのがどこか哀れですらあった。彼の位置と先ほどまで智里が剣を血振りしていた位置、一足跳びに詰められる間合いではない。間には他の仲間たちだって立ち並んでいる。大体先ほど無残にも口惜しくも斬り捨てられたあの者は、仲間のうちでもその鱗[うろこ]硬き事で名高かった者で、なまなか人間の刃などに後れを取る筈がなかったのに。
lines.english: What filled the monster's round, glass-like eyes was not anger or hostility, but a sense of absurd injustice. Almost pitiable. It stood too far from where Tomosato had just shaken his sword clean for a single leap to bridge the gap. Other companions had stood between them too. Besides, the one so cruelly and bitterly cut down moments ago had been renowned among them for his hard scales. No ordinary human blade should have defeated him.

lines.japanese:
その理不尽に戸惑う色、深まった。
　智里と自分を隔てていた仲間が、向こうから順に刈り取られた稲穂ように頽[くずお]れ、倒れた後で様々な斬り口に両断されていた様を見た時に。
　もっとも理不尽に困惑したのは、視界が突然高くなった事だろう。ぽんと宙に投げ飛ばされたような。何事、と叫ぼうとしても声は喉を震わさず。声が通うような喉はなかった。切断された首が地に落ちた時、魚怪の中には有り得べからざる感情が広がりつつあった。
lines.english:
That bewilderment deepened when the companions between it and Tomosato collapsed, one after another from the far end, like reaped rice.
After they fell, it saw the varied cuts that had divided their bodies.
Most bewildering of all, perhaps, was the sudden rise of its own view. As though tossed lightly into the air. What—It tried to cry out, but no voice stirred its throat. No throat remained through which a voice could pass. When the severed head fell to the ground, an emotion that ought not to exist among fish-monsters was spreading.

lines.japanese:
恐怖だ。
　人間に対して抱いた事のない恐怖───
　王が役立たずと嘲罵した人間の殺し屋。
　なるほど、殺すはずだった相手を斬る事もならず、末姫をむざむざ人質に取られた。
　しかし殺し屋はやはり殺し屋なのだった。
　それも、最悪の。自分達への殺し屋。
　この海底の神殿に招き入れるべきではなかったのだと、一体だけ深く嘆いていた魚怪がある。いつの日にか、智里と酒場で相対していた者だ。
lines.english:
Fear.
Fear of a human, such as they had never felt.
The human killer their king had mocked as useless.
Certainly, he had failed to cut down his intended target and allowed the youngest princess to be taken hostage.
Yet a killer remained a killer.
The worst kind:
a killer of them. One fish-monster bitterly regretted having admitted him into this undersea temple. The one who had once faced Tomosato in a tavern.

lines.japanese:
彼は、朋輩の中でも若い者が強硬に、末姫を、泪を連れ戻す事を言い立てる事を憂いていた穏健派であり、それ故に泪の周りにいる智里に接触もしたのだけれど、まず初見で殺し屋の蒼い眸[ひとみ]に怖気を催した。人間が具えていていい目ではない。
　話の中、殺し屋がぼそりと漏らした、
『でも俺[おい]ら、どうしたもんだかな。
　実はよ、あんたらの姫さんの方がどっちかっつうと先口だったんだわ』
　の言葉にも、その時は自分への追従程度だと考えていた。
　いずれにせよ、王が雇うたとはいえ、せいぜい悪くて依頼にしくじり、なんとかと言った、末姫につきまとう猿を殺し損なう程度であろうと、その程度にしか。
　しかし、この有様は、どうだ───

　しかし、この有様は、どうだ───
lines.english:
He belonged to the moderates, troubled by the younger members' forceful insistence on bringing Rui, the youngest princess, home. That was why he had approached Tomosato among those around her. At their first meeting, the killer's blue eyes had frightened him.
Eyes no human should possess.
During the conversation, the killer had murmured,
'But what's a fellow to do? Truth is, your princess had first claim on me, more or less.'
At the time, he had taken it for little more than ingratiation.
The king might hire him, but at worst the commission would fail. He might fail to kill the ape hanging about the princess, whatever his name was. That was all he had imagined.
But what was this—?

lines.japanese: 人間に後れを取る筈もない剛の者が、ろくに爪を合わせもせずに倒れ伏し、なんとか、朔屋か、は、推参にも末姫を人質に取り……人質？　末姫と殺し屋の交誼。殺し屋と朔屋の気安げな有様、つまり───？
lines.english: Warriors who should never have lost to a human fell without even properly crossing claws. The something-or-other—Sakuya?—had presumptuously taken the youngest princess hostage… Hostage? Her connection with the killer. The killer's easy familiarity with Sakuya. In other words—?

lines.japanese: と、事情にある程度通じた、老巧の魚怪でさえようやく事の状況に気がつき始めたくらいだもの、他の魚怪がそれ、まだまだ気づく事はないであろうの、それ。
lines.english: Even this experienced fish-monster, acquainted with some of the circumstances, was only now beginning to understand. The others would surely remain unaware for a while yet.

lines.japanese:
朔屋が、泪の首に腕を巻きつけたまま、広間の出口へと逃げ腰にじりじり進んでいく。
　その前に魚怪たちの列が乱れ、隙間が生ずる。隙を開ける者は、もちろん賊が末姫に一筋でも傷をつけるを恐れた、ある意味では善良な忠義者であるが、彼らは末姫の首に巻かれた腕、なぜああもだらしないのか、なのか、その実に気づいたらどう思ったろうか。その腰、姫を人質に取るような残忍にして非道な者であるにも関わらず、なぜああも臆病に引け腰なのか。
lines.english:
With his arm still about Rui's neck, Sakuya edged timidly toward the hall's exit.
The fish-monsters' ranks broke before him, opening gaps. Those who yielded were, in a sense, good and loyal beings, afraid the villain might inflict even a scratch upon their princess. But what would they think if they understood why the arm around her neck was so slack? Why the hips of a cruel, ruthless hostage-taker drew back so timidly?

lines.japanese:
それ、泪だから。泪が朔屋の腕に手を添えて、巻きつけているように見せているだけだから。腰の事についても、泪が長年の性遍歴の間に覚えたやり方で、臀の肉の柔味で男の逸物をよがらせているだけだから。
　朔屋などは、泪を人質にとっているどころか、この魚怪たちの衆目の中で、公然と愛撫を受けていただけだったのである。
lines.english:
Because it was Rui. Rui had placed her hand on Sakuya's arm and merely made it look as though it was wrapped about her neck. As for his hips, she was using something learned in her long sexual wanderings, pleasuring his member with the soft flesh of her bottom.
Far from holding Rui hostage, Sakuya was simply being caressed openly before the whole assembly of fish-monsters.

lines.japanese: かくしてついに、泪は恐怖のあまりに、引きつらせた顔の、唇の端を奇妙にひくつかせながら。朔屋はこのままだとズボンの中で精漏らしてしまいかねない微妙な快楽から、逃れた方がいいのではないか、でもそんな堅固な意志自分にはあったっけかと情けなくも流されながら、広間の出口より退散を果たす。
lines.english: Thus, at last, Rui, her face contorted with terror, the corners of her lips twitching oddly, withdrew through the hall's exit. Sakuya followed, swept along by a delicate pleasure that threatened to make him spill inside his trousers. Perhaps he ought to escape it. But had he ever possessed such firmness of will?

lines.japanese: 「おおっと、やばいぞう、賊は姫君を連れて逃げてしまったー」
lines.english: “Oh no, this is bad! The villain's escaped with the princess!”

lines.japanese: 智里は追いかける様子を見せたが、さて、朔屋に追いつきそうになる魚怪を見ると、ばっさばっさと切り斃しているのでは話にならない。
lines.japaneseRuby: 智里は追いかける様子を見せたが、さて、朔屋に追いつきそうになる魚怪を見ると、ばっさばっさと切り[R斃^たお]しているのでは話にならない。
lines.english: Tomosato made a show of pursuing them. Yet whenever he saw a fish-monster about to catch Sakuya, he cut it down with a slash. Hardly a convincing performance.

lines.japanese: 岩床に沓[くつ]の踵[かかと]高らかに鳴らし、走る泪に朔屋は、そんな風に愉[たの]しそうに走る泪など見た事がないと、彼女に手を引かれながら呆然となる。常に頽廃的な優雅の極みに漂うてあった泪、世の中の様々な出来事に倦んで、性とカードの遊戯くらいしか、興味を持たなくなった失意の人魚姫。

lines.english: Rui ran with her heels ringing upon the rock. Led by her hand, Sakuya stared in amazement. He had never seen her run with such delight. Rui, always drifting at the height of decadent elegance. The disappointed mermaid princess, weary of the world's events, interested now in little but sex and cards.

それが今やどうだ。堪えきれない笑いが、走る拍子にスタッカートに押し出され、走る事それ自体が愉[たの]しくて、逃げる為という目的を忘れているかの夢中の足取り、髪を乱し、洋装汗に乱させ、円熟した乳房や臀が跳ね回る様など言語道断。
　世界が愉[たの]しい、驚異に満ちて、素晴らしく広い事を知り始めて夢中になる、ありとあらゆる生き物の少女・少年時代が泪の中に再来したかの有様で───

lines.english:
And now? Laughter she could not contain escaped in staccato bursts with each stride. Running itself delighted her. Her absorbed steps seemed to forget that escape was their purpose. Her hair was in disarray, her dress rumpled and damp with sweat; the bouncing of her ripe breasts and bottom was positively scandalous.
It was as though the childhood of every living creature had returned within her: discovering with eager wonder that the world was delightful, marvelous, magnificently wide.

lines.japanese:
逃げる最中に、小休止の為に入りこんだ、小さな一角で。岩肌の影に沈んで、入口は容易に見つかりそうになく、二人が暫[しばら]く息を整える暇くらいは作れそうだった。
　どうやらこの隠れ家のような岩間、泪がかつてこの海底洞にいた際の彼女の秘密の小部屋らしかった。
lines.english:
While fleeing, they slipped into a little recess for a pause. Sunk in the rock's shadow, its entrance seemed unlikely to be found easily. It would give them time to catch their breath.
Apparently this hideout-like gap had been Rui's secret little room when she lived in the undersea cave.

lines.japanese: 「ひどい汗ね、直さん。ほら……」
lines.english: “You're terribly sweaty, Nao. Here…”

lines.japanese:
「ってなあ、泪さん。
　完全に巻きこんだな、俺を」
lines.english:
“Listen, Rui.
You've dragged me into this completely.”

lines.japanese: 泪は殊勝げに押し当ててきた手巾に汗を吸わせつつ、朔屋はどうにも微妙な面持ちの、事のあらましがいい加減見えてきた彼に、ぬけぬけと、浮かべた笑みがまあ素敵だった事。
lines.japaneseRuby: 泪は殊勝げに押し当ててきた[R手巾^ハンケチ]に汗を吸わせつつ、朔屋はどうにも微妙な面持ちの、事のあらましがいい加減見えてきた彼に、ぬけぬけと、浮かべた笑みがまあ素敵だった事。
lines.english: As the handkerchief she pressed to him so dutifully absorbed his sweat, Sakuya wore an uncertain expression. He was finally beginning to see what had happened. The smile she offered him with utter shamelessness was nevertheless splendid.

lines.japanese:
「そういうことになるかしら。
　でも女のすることに巻きこまれる、というのも、素敵な殿方の素養の一つよ」
lines.english:
“Perhaps it amounts to that. But being caught up
in a woman's doings is one of an attractive gentleman's accomplishments.”

lines.japanese: 「……ねえ、直さん」
lines.english: “…Nao.”

lines.japanese: 朔屋の膝に手を置いて、胸元を指でなぞりながら、寄せる顔の静かな、先ほどまでの疾走の間中の汗の名残で僅かに艶[つや]帯びたが、深い風情に翳[かげ]りを帯びた。
lines.english: Resting a hand on his knee and tracing his chest with a finger, she brought her face close. It still gleamed faintly with the sweat of their flight, but was quiet now, with a shadowed gravity to it.

lines.japanese: 「わたくし、途中まではね、お別れを言おうって思っていたのよ」
lines.english: “Until a certain point, I meant to say goodbye.”

lines.japanese:
「どんなにその時は燃え上がっても、いずれ冷えてしまうのが、海と陸の定め。
　二人を退屈の水が冷やしてしまって」
lines.english:
“However fiercely they burn at first, sea and land are fated to cool in time.
The waters of boredom cool them both.”

lines.japanese:
「え……本当は、そんなつもりで……？
　だって、俺、ようやくあなたと、なんというか、馴染み始めた感じなのに……」
lines.english:
“Huh…
You really meant that…? But I've only just begun to feel… comfortable with you…”

lines.japanese:
と朔屋が抱いた危惧は。
　この小さな岩屋の壁が迫り来るような、胸が締め付けられるように痛く、重苦しいものであったのに、同じ岩肌に響いてころころと転がったのは、別離を悼む女の思わしげと言うより、男をからかう事を覚え始めた娘の侠[きゃん]の声。
lines.english:
The fear Sakuya felt was heavy and painful,
as though the little chamber's walls were closing upon him, tightening his chest. Yet the voice that rolled lightly against those same walls sounded less like a woman mourning a parting than a pert woman only just discovering how to tease a man.

lines.japanese: 「───とかなんとか、思いこんでいたのだけれど」
lines.english: “Or something along those lines. That's what I'd convinced myself of.”

lines.japanese:
「……考えを改めました、今日。
　ありがとうね、直さん。
　こんなに愉[たの]しんだのなんて、
　もう思い出せないくらい遠くのこと」
lines.english:
“…Today I changed my mind.
Thank you, Nao.
It's been so long since I enjoyed myself
this much that I can't remember.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ泪さん……あなたさ、もしかして、その、なにか切なげな顔はさ、哀しいとかそういうことではなく、なにかをこらえていらっしゃる？」
lines.english: “Rui… That rather heartbroken expression… Is it not sadness, but you holding something back?”

lines.japanese:
「わかったの。貴方。ただ二人だけでは、
　冷えてしまうのかも知れないけれど」
lines.english:
“I understand now, dear.
Alone, the two of us might cool.”

lines.japanese:
「炎は、風が熾します。直さん。
　わたくし、貴方を守って差し上げますね」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「炎は、風が[R熾^おこ]します。直さん。
　わたくし、貴方を守って差し上げますね」
lines.english:
“Wind stokes a flame.
Nao, I shall protect you.”

lines.japanese:
見ようによっては、哀しげ、運命の無情と愛情という感情の性質を嘆く風情は確かに見えたが、最後の一言。
　一体、何から何を守る、と？
　朔屋の胸中に来したのは、傘も持たないのに、前方にわき起こる黒雲を見た時の不安に等しい。
lines.english:
Looked at one way, she certainly appeared sad, lamenting fate's mercilessness and the nature of love.
But that last remark. Protect what from what?
Sakuya felt the unease of seeing black clouds gathering ahead when one had no umbrella.

lines.japanese:
「頼もしい言葉なのに、
　何やら、不穏な……」
lines.english:
“Such reassuring words.
Yet somehow ominous…”

lines.japanese:
「いつまでもわたくしを追いかけて、嫌い、鬱陶しいと思っていたけれど。
　あの者達を出し抜いた時の、心地好さ」
lines.english:
“I hated their endless pursuit. Found it tiresome.
But the pleasure when we outwitted them…”

lines.japanese:
「……これねえ。
　直さんが私の傍にいて下さる限り、
　いつでも楽しめるのじゃなくって？」
lines.english:
“…Couldn't I enjoy
that whenever I liked,
as long as you stay beside me?”

lines.japanese:
つまり泪は。
　要するに、適度な危険があった方が燃えるじゃない、スリルという、吹く風が強くてあなたが吹き飛ばされそうでも、自分が一緒にいるから、と。
lines.english:
In other words,
Rui meant: a little danger made things burn brighter. Even if the wind of that thrill blew hard enough to sweep him away, she would be with him.

lines.japanese:
「ちょ……泪さん、それは、俺に───
　的になれと───？
　あいつらを引き寄せる為の？」
lines.english:
“Wait… Rui,
are you telling me to be a target?
To draw them in?”

lines.japanese:
「わたくしの傍に、
　いてくださりませんの？」
lines.english:
“Won't you
stay beside me?”

lines.japanese: 朔屋の膝に、胸元に、泪の爪の先が軽く、弱く、時に少しだけ強く食いこむのは、ねだるというのもあったし、朔屋を今更逃しはしないと、自分の刻印を刻んでいるようでもあったし、青年の頬に浮かんだ笑いも、女の深情けにはにかむ色と同時に、落ちるべき処に落ちてしまってもう抜けられない、そんな自分を見いだした、乾いた笑いの。
lines.english: The tips of Rui's nails pressed into Sakuya's knee, into his chest: lightly, faintly, now and then a little harder. There was pleading in it, and also something of carving her seal into him—a declaration that she had no intention of letting him escape now. The smile that rose to Sakuya's face held both the bashfulness of a man receiving a woman's ardent devotion and the dry laughter of one who found himself fallen precisely where he had been bound to fall, with no getting out again.

lines.japanese: 二つの意味を互いに秘めて、寄り添う男と女は、まあそれなりに───愉しそうで、幸せそうで。
lines.japaneseRuby: 二つの意味を互いに秘めて、寄り添う男と女は、まあそれなりに───[R愉^たの]しそうで、幸せそうで。
lines.english: Each concealing two meanings, the man and woman nestled together looked, well, reasonably happy. Reasonably pleased.

lines.japanese:
「そんなに切なげな顔で迫られたって、
　迫られたって……。
　もっと、見せてくれます？」
lines.english:
“Even if you press me with such a sorrowful face…
Even if you
do… Could you show me more of it?”

lines.japanese:
「お側において下さるのなら、
　わたくしは、直さんの為にどんな顔でも。
　どんなことでも」
lines.english:
“If you'll keep me beside you,
any face for you, Nao.
Anything at all.”

lines.japanese:
「でも勘違いなさっちゃいやよ。
　貴方、だからなの。
　貴方以外の殿方と逃避行なんて」
lines.english:
“But don't misunderstand.
It is because it's you.
Fleeing with some other gentleman…”

lines.japanese: 「でも、もし、直さんがわたくしから逃げてしまわれたなら───これほど哀しいことは、在りません」
lines.english: “But if you were to run away from me—nothing could be sadder.”

lines.japanese: 「哀しくて、哀しくて、きっとどこまでも追いかけてしまうことでしょう。わたくしをここまでその気にさせたのだもの」
lines.english: “So sad, so sad, I'd surely pursue you everywhere. You've got me this eager, after all.”

lines.japanese:
どこやら郭の誠めかした言葉を、そのような口ぶりでわざと言う。
　けれど朔屋は、それが泪の深情けだと信じた。長の歳月彷徨った、人魚の姫の誠の心、那辺にあろうとも。それでもこの綺麗な女にここまで言われるのは、心地いい。
　安い偽り？　騙される幸せ？
　ああ、そういうのもどうでもいいのだ。
　寄り添う泪は間違いなく美しく、きっと何時までも変わらずに美しく、そしてこの美しい女を───
lines.japaneseRuby:
どこやら[R郭の誠^くるわのまこと]めかした言葉を、そのような口ぶりでわざと言う。
　けれど朔屋は、それが泪の深情けだと信じた。長の歳月[R彷徨^さまよ]った、人魚の姫の誠の心、那辺にあろうとも。それでもこの綺麗な女にここまで言われるのは、心地いい。
　安い偽り？　騙される幸せ？
　ああ、そういうのもどうでもいいのだ。
　寄り添う泪は間違いなく美しく、きっと何時までも変わらずに美しく、そしてこの美しい女を───
lines.english:
Words somewhat like a courtesan's vows, spoken deliberately in just that manner.
Yet Sakuya believed them to be Rui's deep affection. Wherever the true heart of a mermaid princess who had wandered for so many years might lie, it felt good to have this beautiful woman speak to him so.
A cheap lie?
The happiness of being deceived?
Ah, none of that mattered either. Rui beside him was unquestionably beautiful, surely beautiful forever. And this beautiful woman—

lines.japanese: 「そうときたか。はっはっはっ。もう駄目だ俺。だってさあ、だってさあ、泪さん、あんたそんなでも、綺麗なんだもの、抱きたいって思わせるんだもの」
lines.english: “So that's how it is. Hahaha. I'm finished. Because, because, Rui—even like that, you're beautiful. You make me want to take you in my arms.”

lines.japanese:
この美しい女を抱く事は、抱かれる事は、なによりも素晴らしい、底無しの麻薬のような体だ、溺れて飽きる事はないが、これ以外はなにも満足できなくなってしまうほどの。
　女の手練手管？　男の悲哀？
　ああ、そういうのもどうでもいいのだ。
　なにしろ、泪は始めから言っていたではないか。
lines.english:
To embrace this beautiful woman, to be embraced by her, was more wonderful than anything. A body like a bottomless narcotic. One could drown in it and never tire, until nothing else could satisfy.
A woman's wiles?
A man's sorrow? Ah, none of that mattered either.
Had Rui not said it from the beginning?

lines.japanese: 「───優しく、してね。これから先」
lines.english: “Be gentle with me. From now on.”

lines.japanese:
「ええ、もちろん。
　直さんが望むように。優しく、じわじわと。
　お互いの首を、真綿で絞めるように。
　愉しみましょうねえ……」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「ええ、もちろん。
　直さんが望むように。優しく、じわじわと。
　お互いの首を、真綿で絞めるように。
　[R愉^たの]しみましょうねえ……」
lines.english:
“Yes, of course.
As you wish, Nao. Gently, little by little.
As though strangling each other with soft silk.
Let us enjoy ourselves…”

lines.japanese: そう、泪が言っていたとおりに、愉しむだけでいい。肉の快楽の素晴らしさ、堪能し、そして自分達を追い来たる危難が、味の彩りとなって快楽をより高めてくれよう。
lines.japaneseRuby: そう、泪が言っていたとおりに、[R愉^たの]しむだけでいい。肉の[R快楽^けらく]の素晴らしさ、堪能し、そして自分達を追い来たる危難が、味の彩りとなって[R快楽^けらく]をより高めてくれよう。
lines.english: Yes, as Rui had said, they need only enjoy themselves. Savor the marvel of fleshly pleasure. The dangers pursuing them would lend color to its flavor and heighten it further.

lines.japanese:
───この時、朔屋が、泪のいう、肉の快楽、ただ一つの確かなもの、彼自身がその一つになったのだろう。泪の快楽として。
　そして泪もまた、朔屋の為の唯一最高の快楽として、人魚の肉を差し出して。朔屋はあるいはもしかしたらこの先、どれだけの生を生きる事になるのか、それはわからない、この時は、まだ。
lines.english:
At this moment, perhaps Sakuya himself became one of those pleasures of flesh Rui called the only certain things. A pleasure for Rui.
And Rui, too, offered her mermaid flesh as his single greatest pleasure. And Sakuya—how long might he live from this point on? There was no knowing. Not yet, at that moment.

lines.japanese: 何か自分がとんでもない間違いをやらかしたような気がしてならない朔屋だが、岩屋を出でて逃げるうちに潜水艦を留めてあったところまで辿り着く。
lines.english: Unable to shake the feeling that he had made some tremendous mistake, Sakuya left the rock chamber. In their flight, they reached the place where the submarine had stopped.

lines.japanese: 「よう、二人とも、逃げおおせたようだの」
lines.english: “Hey, you two. Looks like you got away.”

lines.japanese:
「うーん、どうなんだろうなぁ……。
　だってあれ」
lines.english:
“Mm. I wonder… Because,
look…”

lines.japanese:
智里とも合流を果たしたのだけれど、海底洞窟の奥からは、洞窟自体が震動しているのではないかと言うくらいの魚怪たちの雄叫びと、らんらんと光る魚眼がそれこそ津波のように迫り来たる。
　この潜水艦まで逃げ延びてきたけれど、朔屋も泪もこんな巨大な鋼の塊、どう動かすのか見当も付かない。
lines.english:
They had rejoined Tomosato, but cries from the cave's depths were so tremendous that the cave itself seemed to shake. Gleaming fish eyes approached like a great wave.
They had escaped as far as this submarine, yet neither Sakuya nor Rui had any idea how to move such a great lump of steel.

lines.japanese: 「まあいいから。ぐずってねえでハッチ開けて入っていろよ」
lines.english: “Never mind. Stop dawdling, open the hatch, and get in.”

lines.japanese: 重い鋼の蓋の中に二人を押し込め、締め直す前に智里は内部の暗がりに声を張り上げた。
lines.english: He pushed them beneath the heavy steel lid. Before closing it again, he called into the interior darkness.

lines.japanese: 「やい。いるんだろう！？　どこに潜[もぐ]り込んでいるやら知らねえが、お前、いるな？」
lines.english: “Hey! You're there, aren't you? Don't know where you've crawled off to, but you're in there, right?”

lines.japanese: 「だったらこの船、どうにか動かして信天翁まで持って行け」
lines.english: “Then get this ship moving somehow and take it to the Albatross.”

lines.japanese: 「つべこべ言わねえでやれよ、そんくらいできるんだろ、本当は？」
lines.english: “No arguing. Do it. You can manage that much, can't you? Really?”

lines.japanese:
この期に及んで意味不明の物言いだが、もう朔屋たちにその意味を問いただしている暇はない、ハッチを閉じる、ギリギリと締める。
　朔屋が最後に見たモノは、押し寄せる魚怪の大群に、弧剣一振りで対峙する智里の姿。
lines.english:
Incomprehensible words even now, but Sakuya and Rui had no time to ask what they meant. The hatch closed, tightened down.
What Sakuya saw last was Tomosato facing the approaching mass of fish-monsters with a single sword.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ……最低だと言ってくれる女は多いんだが、殺し屋を友達と呼ぶ阿呆は滅多にいなくってさあ」
lines.english: “Well… Plenty of women call me the worst. But not many fools call a killer their friend.”

lines.japanese:
「あとお前、こう後顧の憂いなく大量殺戮の機会なんてそうそうねえぜえ。
　まあそういうこった。
　その人魚姫と達者でな。
　───あばえ！」
lines.english:
“Besides, you don't often get a chance for wholesale slaughter without having to watch your back.
So that's that. Stay well
with your mermaid princess.
Be seeing you!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ後こいつを持ってけ、忘れんな」
lines.english: “Oh, take this too. Don't forget it.”

lines.japanese: ハッチが閉まる寸前に、隙間から投げ込んできた短剣こそが、泪が王子を刺し貫いたものであったのだが、何故智里がそんなモノを持ち出してきたのか、朔屋に渡したのか、それはまだ判らない、今はまだ。
lines.english: Just before the hatch closed, he threw a dagger through the gap. It was the one with which Rui had pierced the prince. Why Tomosato had brought such a thing away, why he gave it to Sakuya, remained unknown. Not yet.

lines.japanese:
……智里はああ叫んだけれど、二人は艦内のどこにも密航者の姿を見つけられず、それにやはりこんな鋼の船の動かしたかたなど判るはずもなく。
　朔屋は、別れる寸前の魚怪たちの圧倒的な数と、智里の姿を想い、やはり耐えきれず、自分などなんの助けにもならないと知りつつも、もう一度ハッチから彼に、一体何を言おうしたのだろう。一体何をしてやろうとしたのだろう。
lines.english:
Tomosato had shouted all that, but the two could find the stowaway nowhere aboard. Nor, naturally, did they know how to operate such a steel vessel.
Thinking of the overwhelming number of fish-monsters at their parting, and Tomosato facing them, Sakuya could not bear it. Knowing he could offer no help, he nevertheless made for the hatch again. What had he intended to say? What had he hoped to do for him?

lines.japanese:
なんにせよその機会は失われた。
　潜水艦が突如また息を吹き返したのである。一体どのような原理で作動しているのか相変わらず判らないが、動いてしまえば泪と朔屋にはもうできる事はない。
　二人で暗がりの中にしゃがみこみ、浮上するまで───言うまでもない。存分に愉[たの]しみ合った。危地を逃れた安堵が、朔屋を異様に昂奮させていたし、泪もまた長きの伴侶得たといたく喜んでいたから。
　───暗がりのどこかから、聞き覚えのある舌打ちが聞こえたような気がしたけれど、二人は気にせず、いや、その気があったら混ざるといいと手招きしたけれど反応がなかったので、そのまま二人で交合[まぐわ]り続けたのだった。
lines.english:
In any case, the chance was lost.
The submarine abruptly came to life again. They still had no notion what principle made the thing run, but once it was under way there was nothing more Rui or Sakuya could do.
They crouched together in the darkness and, until they surfaced—needless to say—took their fill of one another. The relief of escaping danger had excited Sakuya beyond reason, while Rui was overjoyed to have acquired a lasting companion.
They thought they heard a familiar click of the tongue somewhere in the darkness, but paid it no mind—no, they beckoned, inviting whoever it was to join them if so inclined. No answer came, and so the two went on coupling.

lines.japanese:
そうしてその後の二人は、結局、信天翁号から降りてしまった。
　無頼者どもたちとの別れは実にあっさりしたもので、惜しむ愁嘆場も再会の約もなくオンボロ船は港を離れ、彼らたちの流離いに還っていく。
　ただ。信天翁号を降りた二人を待ち受けているのも、結局は。
　似通った日々なのだった。
lines.japaneseRuby:
そうしてその後の二人は、結局、信天翁号から降りてしまった。
　無頼者どもたちとの別れは実にあっさりしたもので、惜しむ[R愁嘆場^しゅうたんば]も再会の約もなくオンボロ船は港を離れ、彼らたちの[R流離^さすら]いに還っていく。
　ただ。信天翁号を降りた二人を待ち受けているのも、結局は。
　似通った日々なのだった。
lines.english:
Afterward, in the end, the two left the Albatross.
Their parting from its lawless company was remarkably brief. No sorrowful scene, no promise to meet again. The dilapidated ship left port and returned to its wandering.
Yet what awaited the pair who had disembarked was, after all,
a similar life.

lines.japanese: ───乗りこんだ車両の、予約していたコンパートメントとは異なる個室だ。先客には幾許かの金で言い含め、しばらく席を外してもらっている。
lines.japaneseRuby: ───乗りこんだ車両の、予約していたコンパートメントとは異なる個室だ。先客には[R幾許^いくばく]かの金で言い含め、しばらく席を外してもらっている。
lines.english: A private compartment in the train they had boarded, not the one they had reserved. A little money had persuaded its previous occupants to step out for a while.

lines.japanese:
個室の椅子に落ち着く、ではなく二人は車窓の窓の下、窓枠からはみ出さないように身を屈めて、共に息を潜[ひそ]める。
　───追っ手は、今日も二人の辿る道を後から、迫ってきている、さて躱[かわ]せるかどうか。
　躱せる。躱せますとも。
　二人ともそれは知っている。
　知っていたとしても、もしや、の想いは何時もつきまとい、それが二人を緊張させる。
　ただその緊張は、二人には必要なものだった。これがないと、日々が引き締まらない。
lines.english:
Rather than settling into the seats, they crouched beneath the window, careful not to show above its frame, holding their breath together.
Their pursuers were following their path again today.
Would they evade them?
They would. Of course they would. Both knew it.
Yet even knowing, the thought of what if always clung to them, keeping them tense.
That tension, however, was something they needed. Without it, their days lacked definition.

lines.japanese:
その後二人は───
　旅から旅の浮き草生活を続けている。魚怪たちの王、泪の父王は諦めた様子はなく、二人に寄せられる追っ手や搦[から]め手も相変わらずで、朔屋は心が安まる暇がない。おそらくはこの女と一緒にいる限り、ずっとこうなのだ。
　だがそのような暮らしでいい、と朔屋は口ではどうであれ、心では受け入れている。
lines.english:
Afterward,
the two continued their drifting life, journey after journey. The fish-monsters' king, Rui's father, showed no sign of giving up. Pursuers and indirect schemes kept coming. Sakuya had no time for peace of mind. Probably it would always be this way,
so long as he stayed with this woman. Yet whatever he said aloud, his heart accepted such a life.

lines.japanese:
「ようやく行ったみたいね。
　しつこいったらありません」
lines.english:
“They seem to have gone at last.
So persistent.”

lines.japanese:
「泪さんよう。今年に入って何度目だ。
　住まいを替えて、こんな風に冷や汗モノで逃げ出すのは」
lines.english:
“Rui, how many times this year?
Changing where we live, then fleeing like this in a cold sweat?”

lines.japanese: 車窓の下に身を屈める朔屋は、彼と向かい合い同じく身を屈める泪へぼやいた。汽車の車窓の向こうには、行き交う黒服の男達、一見しただのマフィアの手下辺りに見えたが、泪の父王の息が掛かっていること、恐らく間違いはない。
lines.english: Crouched beneath the train window, Sakuya complained to Rui, crouched opposite. Beyond the glass, men in black passed to and fro. At first glance they might have been ordinary Mafia henchmen, but they were almost certainly under Rui's father's influence.

lines.japanese: 「わたくしが、そういう勘定などしないって、もうご存じの筈よ」
lines.english: “You ought to know by now that I don't count such things.”

lines.japanese: 「いいじゃない。退屈とは無縁なのだもの」
lines.english: “Isn't it fine? We never have to be bored.”

lines.japanese: 「俺、なんか、どこかで女性というものの事を考え違いしていたかも……」
lines.english: “Maybe… Somewhere along the way… I misunderstood something about women…”

lines.japanese:
やれやれ、と身を起こしたのも、充分に時間を空けてのつもりだったけれど、ホームの端に運悪く追っ手の一人が残っていて、朔屋へと振り向いてくる───寸前で。
　
　泪に手を引かれ、また慌てて車窓の下に潜[もぐ]りこむ。
lines.english:
He rose with a weary sigh, thinking he had allowed enough time. Unfortunately, one pursuer remained at the platform's edge and began turning toward him. Just before he did, Rui pulled Sakuya's hand.
He hastily ducked beneath the window again.

lines.japanese: 「貴方、わたくしから離れてはいけなくってよ。もし離れたら───あっという間に捕まって、よくって八つ裂きにされるわね」
lines.english: “Dear, you mustn't leave me. If you do, you'll be caught at once. Torn into eight pieces, at best.”

lines.japanese: 「貴方がわたくしを人質にしている限りは、お父様も貴方には手出しできないでしょう」
lines.english: “So long as you hold me hostage, Father probably can't lay hands on you.”

lines.japanese: 「だからね、わたくしをずっと人質にしていてね、きっとよ、貴方───」
lines.english: “So keep me your hostage forever. Promise, dear…”

lines.japanese: 「やれやれ……」
lines.english: “Good grief…”

lines.japanese:
船員服を質のいい背広に換えた朔屋、服に着られる口かと思いきやなかなかに嵌る。馬子には衣装で、泪と並べれば似合いの二人、と言って言えなくない。
　そんな連れ合いの、景気悪いぼやきを封じるように、片手の人差し指、朔屋の唇に軽く押し当てて「しぃー……」の泪の仕草、向けられる目線の、軽く細め、唇は内緒話を持ちかけるように軽くすぼめられて、悪戯っぽい、人魚の蠱惑の魅力、汲めど尽きる事のない。
lines.japaneseRuby:
船員服を質のいい背広に換えた朔屋、服に着られる口かと思いきやなかなかに嵌る。馬子には衣装で、泪と並べれば似合いの二人、と言って言えなくない。
　そんな連れ合いの、景気悪いぼやきを封じるように、片手の人差し指、朔屋の唇に軽く押し当てて「しぃー……」の泪の仕草、向けられる目線の、軽く細め、唇は内緒話を持ちかけるように軽くすぼめられて、悪戯っぽい、人魚の蠱惑の魅力、[R汲^く]めど尽きる事のない。
lines.english:
Sakuya had exchanged his sailor's clothes for a good suit. One might have expected it to wear him, but it suited him surprisingly well. Clothes make the man.
With Rui beside him, the two could almost pass for a well-matched couple. As though sealing off her companion's gloomy complaint, she lightly pressed an index finger to his lips. Shh… Her eyes narrowed a little. Her lips pursed as though proposing a secret. Mischievous, the mermaid's beguiling charm could never be exhausted.

lines.japanese:
朔屋は思う。連中は自分をこの女を人質に取ったと思っているようだが、本当はそうではない。
　この女が始めから、自分を自由のための旅券としてとらえたのではないか、と───
　いつからそうするつもりだったのか、そのうち泪に訊ねてみよう。時間は幾らでもある。
　快楽と頽廃の、二人の旅。
　また始まったばかり。
　求める限り、何時までも。
lines.japaneseRuby:
朔屋は思う。連中は自分をこの女を人質に取ったと思っているようだが、本当はそうではない。
　この女が始めから、自分を自由のための旅券としてとらえたのではないか、と───
　いつからそうするつもりだったのか、そのうち泪に訊ねてみよう。時間は幾らでもある。
　快楽と[R頽廃^たいはい]の、二人の旅。
　また始まったばかり。
　求める限り、何時までも。
lines.english:
Sakuya thought. They seemed to believe he had taken this woman hostage, but in truth it was nothing of the kind.
